page.layout: Top: running head and page number; below them two coin medallions side by side, each with a legend around its rim. Below the medallions one page of text in two paragraphs, then a short closing line ("Vide Trebel. Pol."). A woodcut ornament sits in the lower part of the page, below the text.

main_text.p: PISO ad interficiendum Valentem missus, ubi eum providum futurorū imperare cognovit, in Thessaliam concessit, atq; illic paucis sibi cōsentientibus sumpsit Imperiū, Thessalicúsque appellatus, interemptus est, vir frugi, & summæ sanctitatis, dictus ducere originē ab illa Pisonū familia, cui se Cicero nobilitandi causa sociaverat. Ipse quoq; Valens, qui ad eum percussores misisse perhibetur, dixisse fertur, Non sibi apud Deos inferos constare rationem, quòd quamuis hostem suum, Pisonem tamen iussisset occidi, virum cui similem Romana respublica non haberet.

ÆMILIANVS coactus sumpsit Imperium, cùm alioquin videret ob seditionē obortam undecunque sibi pereundum. Consenserunt ei Ægyptiacus exercitus, maximè in Gallieni odium. Nec ei ad regendam rempublicam animus defuit. Nam Thebaidem, totámque Ægyptum peragravit: & quatenus potuit, barbarorum gentes armis ac auctoritate submovit. Denique Alexander, vel Alexandrinus, virtutum merito vocatus est. At cùm contra Indos pararet expeditionem, misso Theodoto duce, Gallieno iubente, dedit pœnas: siquidem strangulatus in carcere, captivorū veterum more, perhibetur.

page.notes: Legends of the two coin medallions (Piso Frugi, Aemilianus) are printed inside the engravings and transcribed above as lines. A stray short mark ("\") lies between the two paragraphs, probably a printer's or scan artefact, not transcribed. A woodcut ornament (square floral pattern) sits at the bottom of the page and carries no text. No marginal notes. Printed "s" and "f" long-s forms normalised to s; u/v and i/j normalised per the rules. Printed spellings such as "cognouit" and "vndecunque" were changed to cognovit and undecunque as u/v normalisation.
